messages:
sandeep: quick heads-up — after last runtime change I’m seeing a regression in tail latency for continuous batching on a subset of tenants. looks like kernel swap + batchcap interaction. sharing initial notes below.

maria: can you paste the loadconfig and a short perf snippet? is this replay harness or synthetic?

sandeep: replay harness. replayed N=10k sessions from prod-sampled trace with tenant mix 60/30/10. command we used:
```
./replay_harness --trace=trace_2026-02-12.json --tenants=multi.yaml --concurrency=300 --duration=10m
```
observed: p95 token latency jumped from ~85ms -> ~210ms for tenant group B after the kernel-selection change. p50 barely moved.

jakob: interesting — p95 spike + p50 stable usually suggests increased tail waiting (queueing) not kernel perf cost. any KV-cache hit rate changes?

sandeep: yes, KV hit-rate for B dropped 12% during the run. curious correlation: when kernel swap decided a different GEMM kernel for long sequences we saw longer serialization in the scheduling path, causing microbursts that pushed B behind.

lina: can we rule out loadframe mismatch between replay and synthetic? i.e., synthetic uses fixed seq dist; replay has a long-tail of seq lengths. apples-to-apples matters here.

chao: we should run an apples-to-apples where synthetic mimics the replay seq-length pdf + tenant arrival process. also stress batch size caps: try batch_cap=16,32,64 and max_delay_ms=2,5,15. small caps often reduce queue depth but increase kernel inefficiencies.

maria: agreed. jacob, do we have profiling to show where time is spent (scheduling vs kernel exec vs memcpy)? a flame or perf counters would help.

jakob: pushed a quick sampled flame from the failing run (summarized):
- 45% scheduler wait/lock contention (pick_batch + policy checks)
- 30% kernel enqueue/serialize overhead (kernel selection path + launching ops)
- 15% actual kernel execution
- 10% memcpy/copy
this screams scheduling-level regression after the kernel-selection change.

sandeep: yep. my theory: the kernel-selection now examines seq_len distribution and quantization flags per-request which is slightly expensive. under high arrival burstiness that per-request decision becomes a contention hot path -> increases head-of-queue latency -> KV cache for B misses more often since prefixes expire while waiting.

lina: actionable plan: (1) instrument kernel-selection to cache decision per-model-version/seq_bucket (cheap map lookup), (2) run apples-to-apples synthetic replay with same seq pdf and tenant skew, (3) sweep batch_cap in {16,32,48,64} and max_delay_ms in {2,5,10,20}, (4) collect KV hit traces and per-tenant tail latencies.

chao: +1. also try a micro-optim: compute kernel-choice lazily only when batch is about to form (amortize). fallback: precompute a compact kernel-key for common (model,quant,seq_bucket) and use it during scheduling.

infra-bot: loadtest job queued: job_id=jt-9123, config=multi-tenant-seqpdf-32cap-5ms, expected duration=10m. link: https://ci.redwood/run/jt-9123

maria: please include the replay vs synthetic diff metric in the run artifacts: per-tenant p50/p95/p99, kv_hit_rate, avg_batch_size, scheduling_lock_time. makes debugging easier.

sandeep: will do. i'll run the sweep tonight and post a short table in the morning. if cache for kernel-choice helps, we should get p95 back within 10% of baseline.

jakob: thanks — if the micro-opt doesn’t close it we should consider relaxing batch_cap for tenant-B at the router level or adding tiny request-class priorities to reduce unfairness.

lina: re: fairness — add a metric to highlight when one tenant's p95 exceeds cluster p95 by >2x. that will help detect future regressions quickly.

sandeep: noted. will upload results to the run artifact and follow up in morning. :heatmap:
